title: OpenAI's Sam Altman briefly changes name to Ram Altman on X
excerpt: Altman renamed himself 'Ram Altman' in a joke reference to the memory shortage that's the talk of the AI industry right now.
content_html:
Sam Altman joked about AI's thirst for memory with a new social media nickname

By Georgia Hennessy

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman briefly gave himself a new name on X: "Ram Altman."

The change followed a joke about his appetite for computer memory after recent controversial comments on how the much-desired memory is allocated.

Responding to an Altman post about people retaining control over AI’s future, an X user wrote "sam come here come here" alongside an image of several memory chips leading toward a cardboard box propped up like a trap.

Altman replied, "i lol’d."

When another user asked whether he could rename his account "Ram Altman,” he answered, "OK yeah" — and did.

The change was short-lived. By 11 a.m. ET on Wednesday, the CEO's name had reverted to "Sam Altman" on his X profile.

It was unclear why he changed it back and OpenAI declined to comment when contacted by Business Insider.

Altman's joke landed after recent remarks about the world’s limited supply of DRAM, a type of memory that is key to both personal computing and the GPUs that power AI data centers.

On an October 29 episode of the "Cheeky Pint" podcast, he argued that running AI models on personal computers could leave scarce memory underused. In a market where supply is tight, he said, cloud data centers can use it more intensively.

Sam Altman joined John Collison for a pint to discuss the scaling laws of agent teams, proving Navier-Stokes, why hand-written software will soon look quaint, the optics of token pricing, and what computing looks like beyond the keyboard and screen.

00:00:00 Introduction… pic.twitter.com/q7jsLCszLW

— Cheeky Pint (@CheekyPint) October 29, 2026

The comments drew criticism from some people who took them to mean consumers should have less access to memory so data centers could have more.

Elon Musk, who has feuded with Altman for years, weighed in on Sunday, posting a meme on X with the caption: "The people deserve to have their RAM too!"

Altman used the X exchange to push back on the topic.

but only because...i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context.

i have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.

— Ram Altman (@sama) November 4, 2026

He said he wants the world to have "tons of memory" and for people to put as much as they want in their computers.

He added that he has long argued for increasing memory production and was annoyed that his remarks had been taken out of context.

When another user asked why he wanted their RAM, Altman replied: "I want you to have so much ram let's build more."

i want you to have so much ram

lets build more

— Ram Altman (@sama) November 4, 2026

Altman’s clarification points to the billion-dollar question beneath it: how to meet demand for memory in both data centers and personal computers.

His answer, at least on X, was to make more of it.
